what_it_does: The software layer between human commanders and fleets of uncrewed/autonomous platforms (air, ground, surface, undersea, launched effects, loitering munitions). It (1) exposes each vehicle's state and payload data to a controller/COP, (2) lets a human or an automated planner assign missions, tasks and rules of engagement to one or many heterogeneous vehicles (task allocation, route/behavior selection, human-on-the-loop approval), (3) coordinates collaborative behaviors between vehicles (relay, search, track, strike) including when links to the operator are degraded or denied, (4) manages fleet identity, health, airspace/waterspace deconfliction and blue-force tracking, and (5) publishes vehicle-derived tracks and sensor data into existing C2/fires systems (TAK, FAAD C2/IBCS, Maven, NGC2, Link 16). It sits above vehicle flight/autonomy stacks (PX4/AuterionOS, Hivemind/EdgeOS, Lattice on-vehicle, FANTOM Core) and below joint C2. In practice it is five sub-layers: on-vehicle mission autonomy; vehicle-to-controller protocol; ground/common control station; multi-vehicle orchestration/task allocation; and C2/COP integration.

sub_taxonomy.name: On-vehicle mission autonomy and collaborative behaviors
sub_taxonomy.note: Software running on the platform (Shield AI Hivemind/EdgeOS, Anduril Lattice on-vehicle, Auterion AuterionOS/Nemyx, Applied Intuition/EpiSci, government-owned SOCOM FANTOM Core, USAF A-GRA-conformant autonomy). Government increasingly asserts ownership of the reference architecture (A-GRA, FANTOM Core) while vendors supply behaviors. FACT (A-GRA, FANTOM Core from 2026 sources).

sub_taxonomy.name: Vehicle-to-controller interface protocols
sub_taxonomy.note: MAVLink (commercial small UAS, PX4/ArduPilot), STANAG 4586 (NATO UAS control interface, Levels of Interoperability 1-5), UMAA (Navy maritime DDS-based service architecture, PMS 406), IOP/JAUS (Army ground robots), UCI/OMS (USAF Open Mission Systems / Universal C2 Interface), Cursor-on-Target (TAK). Mandated open standards exist per domain but are inconsistently enforced across programs; commercial small-drone fleets largely arrive with vendor apps. INFERENCE.

sub_taxonomy.name: Control station / common controller
sub_taxonomy.note: Where the operator sits: vendor GCS apps (AeroVironment/Tomahawk Kinesis, Auterion Mission Control, Anduril Lattice UI), government efforts to own it (Navy Common Control System, NAVAIR PMA-263 Unmanned Common Controller sources sought, Army Universal Robotic Controller study, older BCT Common Controller). The recurring 15-year pattern of common-controller efforts without a universal fielded controller is the clearest proto-purgatory signal in this segment. FACT/INFERENCE.

sub_taxonomy.name: Multi-vehicle orchestration / mission-level tasking
sub_taxonomy.note: Vehicle-agnostic assignment and coordination of many heterogeneous systems: Anduril Lattice for Mission Autonomy (Replicator selection Nov 2024), Auterion Nemyx (multi-manufacturer swarm, launched Sept 2025), Shield AI multi-aircraft Hivemind for CCA, and the DIU/DAWG/Navy Autonomous Vehicle Orchestrator prize challenge (Jan 2026, up to $100M) explicitly seeking a vehicle-agnostic C2 layer. FACT.

sub_taxonomy.name: Integration into existing C2, fires and counter-UAS
sub_taxonomy.note: Publishing autonomy-derived tracks and accepting tasking from COP/fires/C-UAS systems: TAK/ATAK, FAAD C2 (Northrop) and its planned replacement by Lattice as common C-UAS C2 (JIATF-401, March 2026), IBCS, Maven Smart System, Army NGC2, Ukraine Delta as the reference model for a drone-fed kill web. FACT.

sub_taxonomy.name: Autonomy test, evaluation, simulation and data
sub_taxonomy.note: Simulation-based validation of collaborative behaviors, conformance to A-GRA/UMAA/IOP, flight-test data capture, and post-mission exploitation of vehicle logs for ML. Applied Intuition is the commercial reference; government T&E capacity is a known constraint. INFERENCE.

current_architecture.description: Fragmented by domain and vendor. Small commercial drones use MAVLink/PX4-derived stacks with vendor apps; Army Group 2-3 UAS and launched effects use STANAG 4586-style GCS software from platform vendors plus emerging common controllers (Kinesis, Lattice); Navy uses UMAA on-vehicle services with CCS for operator control; Air Force CCA uses a government reference architecture (A-GRA) with vendor mission autonomy. Multi-vehicle orchestration is delivered mostly by Anduril Lattice (Replicator/DAWG, SOCOM, Army C-UAS), with Auterion Nemyx and Shield AI Hivemind as multi-vehicle alternatives, and the government now trying to procure a vehicle-agnostic orchestrator (AVO prize challenge). Integration to the COP is typically via TAK/CoT, Link 16/JREAP gateways, or vendor APIs. Human-on-the-loop remains the policy default; engagement approval flows through fires/C-UAS systems rather than the autonomy layer.

technical_difficulty.summary: High. Real-time coordination of heterogeneous vehicles across radios with intermittent links, safety-critical engagement logic with human-on-the-loop, deterministic behavior under GNSS/comms denial, and integration with dozens of legacy protocols. Individual pieces (MAVLink control, mission planning UIs, CoT publishing) are commodity; the hard parts are certifiable multi-vehicle behaviors, DDIL-tolerant state synchronization, and trustworthy delegation of engagement authority.
required_expertise: distributed systems and consensus under partition
robotics/autonomy (behavior trees, task allocation, path planning)
tactical datalinks and mesh radio behavior
safety assurance and T&E for autonomy (A-GRA/UMAA conformance)
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Vehicle-agnostic orchestration that survives denied links while keeping a human accountable for lethal effects, across vendors who each control their own autonomy stack and controller. The DIU/DAWG/Navy AVO prize challenge exists precisely because no fielded vehicle-agnostic layer has been accepted. INFERENCE
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: MAVLink/PX4 control, basic GCS UIs, video streaming, CoT/TAK plugins, cloud mission logging, simulation with Gazebo/AirSim-style tools; Blue UAS-listed airframes and radios.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC: software-only orchestration or integration demo using COTS Blue UAS drones and MAVLink in simulation plus a few live vehicles; two founders plus 1-2 engineers for 6-9 months. Credible demo: participation in an Army/Navy/AUKUS experiment or a DIU/DAWG challenge with 5-20 vehicles from at least two vendors, rugged edge compute, mesh radios, safety case, travel and range costs, and early cleared/US-person hires. First production: ATO/CMMC/IL5 accreditation, ITAR compliance program, integration into Lattice/TAK/NGC2 or FAAD C2 successors, 24/7 support, and hardware kits for a battalion-scale fleet. Ranges are HYPOTHESIS calibrated on Auterion ($130M Series B to scale production) and typical defense software startups.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - MAVLink/PX4 fleets, Blue UAS hardware and simulated missions allow an unclassified prototype; realistic tasking doctrine, threat behaviors and datalink parameters are CUI/ITAR
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Not for PoC; needed for credible demo: unit CONOPS, radio configurations, C2 message formats (VMF/Link 16), and access to government reference architectures (A-GRA, FANTOM Core, UMAA specs are partly public via AUVSI).
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Military drone autonomy and C2 software is very likely ITAR-controlled (USML Cat VIII(h)/XI(d) technical data) or EAR 600-series; commercial PX4-based work may be EAR99 until specifically designed for military use. Needs specialist counsel; do not rely on this note.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes as soon as integration with government C2 or program-specific behaviors begins; CMMC Level 2 likely required for DoD contracts handling CUI.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes for CCA, C-UAS C2, Navy fleets and any fires integration; SECRET facility or partnering with a cleared prime/integrator required.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not required for PoC; at least one cleared US-person lead is practically required by the credible-demo stage.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian founder who is not a US person cannot receive ITAR technical data without a DDTC license (deemed export), which typically excludes them from the autonomy behaviors, datalink and C2-integration code; a German founder who becomes a lawful permanent resident is a US person for ITAR and counts toward SBIR ownership. SBIR/STTR requires >50% ownership by US citizens or permanent residents; FOCI mitigation would be needed for a facility clearance if a non-US person holds significant ownership or control. Structure options (US-person majority, walled-off roles, EAR99 commercial line first) require specialist export-control and immigration counsel; no legal judgment is made here.

why_not_solved.explanation: Each platform vendor (AeroVironment, GA-ASI, Anduril, Shield AI, Auterion) ships its own controller and autonomy stack; the controller is where vendor lock and data ownership live, so incentives oppose a neutral orchestrator. Anduril's success has made Lattice the de facto common layer for several buyers, which is itself a proprietary answer.

Air (PEO Aviation, AFLCMC), maritime (PMS 406, NAVAIR), ground (PEO GCS), SOF (SOCOM), C-UAS (JIATF-401) and OSD (DIU/DAWG) each own standards and controllers; no single buyer can mandate one layer, hence parallel A-GRA, UMAA, IOP, FANTOM Core, STANAG 4586.

Cheap edge compute, mesh radios and mature open flight stacks (PX4/MAVLink) only enabled multi-vendor collaborative autonomy at scale around 2023-2025 (Nemyx Dec 2025 demo; CCA autonomy flight tests Feb 2026).

Lethal effects with delegated autonomy require safety cases, human-on-the-loop policy compliance (DoDD 3000.09) and airworthiness/range approvals; every vendor integration re-triggers T&E, slowing any universal layer.

Fielded C2 (FAAD C2, IBCS, TAK, Link 16, NGC2) and dozens of radios/waveforms must be bridged; each bridge is bespoke and CUI/classified, so open-source or commercial-only players cannot finish the last mile.

Partially: for C-UAS tactical C2 and CCA mission autonomy the government has picked production vendors (Anduril; Anduril/Shield AI/Collins). What remains unsolved is cross-service, cross-vendor orchestration and squad-to-battalion small-UAS fleet control and deconfliction.

attractiveness.bull: The FY2027 DAWG request ($54.6B) and Drone Dominance (200,000 drones by 2027) create unprecedented budget signal for software that orchestrates and integrates mass; the government is actively procuring vehicle-agnostic C2 (AVO challenge, UCC sources sought, FANTOM Core M2M APIs) and asserting open reference architectures, which lowers the moat around incumbents' controllers; integration, deconfliction and training tooling for the small-UAS long tail is fragmented and under-served.
attractiveness.bear: The core orchestration layer is being won by Anduril (Replicator/DAWG, SOCOM, Army enterprise agreement, CCA) with Shield AI and Auterion as scaled alternatives, all with hundreds of millions in capital and cleared workforces; the government's own reference architectures (A-GRA, FANTOM Core, UMAA) further commoditize the layer a startup would sell; ITAR/CUI make a mixed US/non-US founding team structurally constrained at exactly the code that matters; common-controller efforts have cycled for 15 years without production, a proto-purgatory warning; $250k buys a PoC only.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low for a direct orchestration or common-controller play; medium for narrow adjacent wedges (small-UAS fleet integration/deconfliction into unit C2, autonomy T&E/conformance tooling, autonomy data pipelines) that can be built commercially first and sold into or alongside Lattice/TAK/A-GRA ecosystems.

market_stage.rationale: Within ~5 years the segment moved from RFIs and standards to prototype awards (2024) and, by 2026, production-style awards for two sub-layers (C-UAS tactical C2, CCA mission autonomy). Cross-domain vehicle-agnostic orchestration remains at prize-challenge/prototype stage, and small-UAS fleet control is being fielded faster than the C2 layer around it. Hence Transitioning, not Mature.

proto_purgatory.notes: The common-controller sub-layer shows classic purgatory: BCT Common Controller (2010s), Navy CCS, Army URC study, PMA-263 UCC sources sought, ROS-M and IOP - repeated efforts, no universal fielded controller. Replicator itself was dissolved after ~2 years without delivering the promised mass and re-launched as DAWG with a new orchestrator challenge. By contrast, C-UAS C2 and CCA autonomy have reached production awards, showing purgatory is sub-layer-specific.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for any startup whose product is the universal controller or orchestrator sold to the government as a program of record; opportunity for tooling that makes whichever controller wins interoperable, testable and trainable (adapters, conformance, deconfliction, data), sold to primes/integrators and units.

candidate_gaps.title: Vehicle-agnostic orchestration layer (the AVO problem)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: No fielded, government-owned or neutral layer can task and coordinate heterogeneous autonomous vehicles from multiple vendors across domains, so DIU/DAWG/Navy are paying a prize challenge for one.
candidate_gaps.user: DAWG/SOCOM planners, Navy unmanned task units, Army launched-effects commanders
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Each vehicle family arrives with its own GCS/app; 2) operators run several controllers side by side; 3) tasks are coordinated verbally or via TAK chat; 4) tracks are manually re-entered into the COP or bridged by a vendor gateway (Lattice) where available; 5) engagement approval runs in a separate fires/C-UAS system.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Anduril Lattice for Mission Autonomy (Replicator/DAWG, SOCOM); Auterion Nemyx for multi-manufacturer small drones; Shield AI Hivemind for multi-aircraft; government reference stacks (A-GRA, FANTOM Core, UMAA).
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Vendor lock at the controller; each new vehicle needs a bespoke integration; cross-domain (air-sea-ground) tasking not vendor-neutral; DDIL behavior differs per stack.

candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A thin, open, protocol-translation and task-allocation kernel (MAVLink/STANAG 4586/UMAA/CoT) that primes and government labs adopt as a conformance reference rather than a competing product.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-source-style adapter framework demonstrating one mission (relay + search) across three vehicle stacks in simulation, then live with two Blue UAS airframes, published against A-GRA/UMAA-like interfaces; enter via AVO challenge or an AFWERX/xTech SBIR.

candidate_gaps.killer_risk: The government selects Lattice or a government-owned kernel as the answer, leaving no room; two-founder team cannot field DDIL-grade multi-vehicle autonomy safely.

candidate_gaps.title: Blue-force drone identification and deconfliction inside counter-UAS C2
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: As friendly small-drone density explodes, C-UAS operators cannot reliably distinguish friendly autonomous drones from hostile ones in real time, creating fratricide and hesitation risk.
candidate_gaps.user: C-UAS operators (FAAD C2 / Lattice C-UAS), battalion air defense and drone team leaders, JIATF-401
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Friendly drone launches announced by voice/chat; 2) C-UAS sensors detect track; 3) operator correlates manually with known friendly flights and airspace measures; 4) engagement decision made under time pressure; 5) EW effects may also jam friendly links.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Procedural control (airspace boxes, timing), some Remote-ID-like beaconing, vendor-specific IFF, manual correlation in FAAD C2/Lattice.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No standardized, secure, low-bandwidth blue-drone identity feed shared between vendor controllers and C-UAS C2; EW-denied conditions remove cooperative signals.
